newsitem.title: USA: First of America to sell 20 branches.
newsitem.headline: First of America to sell 20 branches.

text.p: First of America Bank Corp, a $22 billion asset bank holding company, said Friday it intends to sell a total of 20 branches in Michigan and Illinois which will result in a gain to fourth quarter earnings of $0.20 to $0.25 a share.
First of America said it intends to sell 15 branches in Michigan, including eight branches previously announced in August and five in Illinois, over the remainder of 1996.
Gains from the branch sales should add about $20 million to $25 million to fourth quarter's non-interest income and raise earnings per share by about $0.20 to $0.25, it said.
Sale of the branches is part of the company's ongoing strategy to streamline its operations.

"We continue to analyze our branch network and retail delivery systems in order to bring products and services directly and profitably to our customers the way they want them delivered," said Richard Chormann, chairman, president and chief executive officer of First of America.

"These steps provide us with the opportunity to increase the efficiency of our product distribution system going forward, and with the opening of 25 supermarket branches during the first six months of 1996, reinvest in new delivery channels," he said.

During the first quarter of 1996, First of America sold three branches in Illinois and one in Michigan resulting in $4.4 million in gains. The additional branch sales will reduce total deposits by about $375 million, or two percent.
First of America has $15 billion in loans and $18 billion in deposits and serves over 3.2 million households in Michigan, Indiana, Illinois and Florida.
